sections.content:
You know *sino* and *sino que* from B1 Unit 40: after a negative they replace the first idea with another (*No es azul, sino verde*). You also know *no es que… sino que* from B2 Unit 5. This lesson sets *sino* beside two phrases that say "instead of" without needing a negative: *en vez de* and *en lugar de*.

• *sino* needs a negative before it: *No compré el libro, sino la revista.* Before a conjugated verb, use *sino que*.
• *en vez de* and *en lugar de* mean the same. *En lugar de* is a little more formal. No negative is needed, and a noun or an infinitive follows: *En vez de comprar el libro, compré la revista.*

When both verbs have the same subject, the first one stays in the infinitive: *en vez de quedarme*, not *en vez de me quedé*.

sections.title: Three ways to replace
rows: No fui al cine, sino al teatro.
I didn't go to the cinema, but to the theatre.
No lo llamé, sino que le escribí un mensaje.
I didn't call him; I wrote him a message instead.
En vez de comprar el libro, compré la revista.
Instead of buying the book, I bought the magazine.
En lugar de llamar, le escribí un mensaje.
Instead of calling, I wrote him a message.

sections.content: *Sino* corrects what you denied, and *pero* only adds an objection: *No es caro, sino barato* is odd, but *No es caro, pero es lejos* is fine. If there is no negative, use *en vez de* or *en lugar de*.
